stories.title: NVIDIA tutorial separates obstacle avoidance from a frozen walking policy
stories.credit: NVIDIA authors on Hugging Face, Nov. 24, 2026
stories.alt: Conceptual Microduck architecture showing time-of-flight observations feeding an avoidance controller, which adjusts commands passed to a frozen walking policy.
stories.facts: NVIDIA’s Microduck tutorial trains a separate obstacle-avoidance controller while keeping a walking policy fixed. Isaac Lab and Newton support simulation, sensor modeling, evaluation and deployment preparation; training includes noise, delay and missing measurements.
stories.inference: For MATLAB trading research, separate a signal policy from execution and independent risk controls, and stress imperfect observations before deployment.
stories.uncertainty: A robotics tutorial, not evidence of trading profitability. Simulation and hardware behavior can differ; the architectural analogy requires financial validation.

stories.title: Graph-informed factor research highlights the cost hurdle in statistical arbitrage
nodes:
Remove major factors
Build residual graph

Trading-cost stress
Net edge can vanish
stories.alt: Conceptual statistical-arbitrage pipeline showing factor removal, residual-graph attention and a transaction-cost stress step that can eliminate the apparent edge.
stories.facts: The preprint builds a signed stock network after removing dominant correlation modes, then uses graph attention in a deep factor model. Its historical U.S. equity tests report improved residual-arbitrage performance, but net Sharpe becomes negative at five basis points per unit traded.
stories.inference: Require an identity-graph ablation, equally tuned PCA benchmark and net-cost acceptance gate before adopting graph complexity.
stories.uncertainty: Unreplicated backtests covering 2015–2024. The headline results are gross of costs; borrow, impact, capacity and realistic fills remain implementation questions.

stories.title: Wall Street pares Wednesday’s losses before the Thanksgiving closure
stories.date: November 25, 2026 cash close; AP report 3:17 p.m. CST
stories.alt: Common-zero chart of rounded November 25 cash-session index changes: Dow plus 0.3%, S&P 500 minus 0.3%, Nasdaq Composite minus 0.6%; prior-close data, not futures or ETF returns.
stories.facts: AP reported Wednesday closes of about +0.3% for the Dow, −0.3% for the S&P 500 and −0.6% for the Nasdaq Composite after substantial intraday losses were pared.
stories.inference: Evaluate Friday’s gap and liquidity afresh rather than treating Wednesday’s late recovery as an execution signal.
stories.uncertainty: Rounded reported index returns, not SPY/QQQ returns or live holiday-session prices. The intraday recovery does not establish a durable reversal.

stories.title: October PCE inflation reaches 3.8% year over year
stories.credit: BEA, October Personal Income and Outlays, Nov. 25
stories.alt: Reported-data panel showing October headline PCE inflation of 3.8% year over year, core PCE of 3.3%, and monthly increases of 0.3% for both measures.
stories.facts: BEA reported October PCE inflation of 3.8% year over year and core PCE inflation of 3.3%. Both price indexes increased 0.3% from September.
stories.inference: Stress rate-sensitive signals against persistent inflation and preserve release vintages; this is the result that was still unknown at yesterday’s cutoff.
stories.uncertainty: Economic estimates can be revised. The release does not by itself determine the next FOMC decision or the future inflation path.

stories.title: HP reports revenue growth while quarterly adjusted EPS declines
stories.credit: HP Inc. fiscal 2026 results release, Nov. 24
nodes:
Q4 revenue
Up 9.3% year over year
stories.alt: Reported-results panel contrasting HP’s fourth-quarter revenue growth of 9.3% with a 10.8% decline in non-GAAP EPS, noting that EPS includes tariff refunds.
stories.facts: HP reported fourth-quarter revenue growth of 9.3% year over year while non-GAAP EPS declined 10.8%. Its fiscal-year EPS measures included favorable tariff refunds.
stories.inference: Test earnings quality and margins separately from top-line hardware demand; isolate nonrecurring items before extrapolating profitability.
stories.uncertainty: Company-reported results using both GAAP and non-GAAP measures. Revenue growth alone does not establish sustainable earnings growth or a stock-price response.
